title: Rapid evals catch-up notes (Jordan)
content:
Context: quick midweek sync with Avery + Sofia. Focus: triage a small quality regression from the last AB run and decide whether to canary rollback or push remediation. These are my prep notes and action checklist — messy, meant for quick reference in the 1:1 and followup.

High-level observations:
- AB result summary (last run, 6/12): variant B shows -3.8% accept_rate on conversational intents vs baseline (stat sig p=0.04). Latency roughly equal (+~5ms). Token cost slightly down (~1.2%).
- Failure modes clustered: factuality hallucinations on multi-hop prompts; truncation/early stop on very long context (>1200 tokens); style drift for onboarding prompts (tone too terse).
- Prompt set: we ran prompt-set v23 (changes: added system hint to be concise, swapped rerank model from emb-v2->emb-v3). Baseline was v21.

Questions to raise in meeting:
- Do we trust the p=0.04 signal given smaller sample for onboarding funnel? (n=1.2k onboarding vs n=12k general) -> ask Avery for sample split.
- Was there any infra change or kernel swap around 6/10-6/12 that could explain deterministic behavior? (SRE/infra blame to check)
- Which customers saw the onboarding tone change? Any high-traffic customers pinned to v23? (product/customer-success to flag)

Quick triage steps (order-of-operations for meeting):
1) Confirm sample breakdown by intent (Avery) — onboard vs auth vs search.
2) Pull 50 representative diffs (baseline vs B) for hallucination examples; manually label severity 0/1/2 (me + Sofia) — aim: <30 min.
3) Check prompt-set diffs: look at system prompt lines changed in v22->v23; highlight possible concise/hallucination tradeoffs.
4) Run targeted small AB with only system prompt reverted (keep emb-v3) on a 2k sample for onboarding prompts — quick sanity.
5) If regression persists after revert-of-system-hint, try embedding rerank threshold bump (0.78->0.82) as mitigation; monitor accept_rate.

Immediate red flags (if true -> rollback):
- >5% drop in accept_rate for onboarding with p<0.01.
- Any customer-facing SLA/uptime incidents correlated with rollout time window.

Proposed experiments (if we avoid immediate rollback):
- Short canary that pins baseline system hint but uses emb-v3 (isolate embedding change effect).
- Small calibration sweep: temperature {0.0, 0.3, 0.7}, presence_penalty {0,0.1}, max_tokens cap at 1024 vs 1536 — measure truncation regressions.
- Automatic AB tagging: label examples that trigger hallucination keywords and route to stricter prompt variant.

Notes-to-self / prep tasks before 1:1 (Jordan):
- Collect the 50 diffs and put into shared gist for quick walkthrough (target: 1 hour prep).
- Prepare a one-slide summary with metric deltas and top 3 example pairs.
- Draft message for CS if we decide to rollback (clear, non-alarmist): include timeframe, root_cause hypothesis, next steps.

Follow-up action items (post-meeting):
- Jordan: run canary AB (system prompt revert) on 2k onboarding set + report by EOD (JUN16).
- Avery: confirm sample splits and retest p-values with bootstrapped CIs (due JUN16).
- Sofia: manual label 50 diffs, flag top 5 severe hallucinations, create tickets (optimize/hallucination-branch) (due JUN17).
- SRE contact (cc: infra): confirm no kernel/driver changes in rollout window (Avery to ping infra) (due JUN16).
- Product: identify any customers pinned to v23 and prepare outreach list if rollback happens (Sofia) (due JUN17).

If rollback plan approved:
- Rollback procedure: patch deployment to point rollout policy -> baseline-model on 10% canary for 30m -> monitor accept_rate and latency -> escalate to full rollback at 10% degradation.
- Communication: short CS note + internal postmortem stub (owner: Jordan) to be filled within 48h.

Misc notes / loose thoughts:
- Maybe emb-v3 lowered similarity in some multi-hop queries; consider rerunning offline nearest-neighbor sanity on KB snippets.
- Could be overfitting to brevity hint: the system prompt that enforces concision may truncate reasoning. Consider conditional brevity: only for intents with short expected answer.
- Add a quick try: add a trailing instruction "preserve reasoning steps if >1 hop" as an experiment.

Timing/meeting agenda (15–20m):
- 0–3m: quick metric recap (Avery)
- 3–8m: show 5 example diffs (Jordan/Sofia)
- 8–12m: decide immediate mitigation (rollback vs canary experiments)
- 12–18m: assign tasks + ownership + deadlines
- 18–20m: align on comms (CS/SRE/Product)

End-of-doc quick checklist (to tick during/after meeting):
- [ ] sample split confirmed
- [ ] 50 diffs collected
- [ ] canary AB kicked off
- [ ] SRE infra verification
- [ ] CS outreach list
- [ ] followup 48h postmortem slot

Random reminder: keep notes informal during meeting — capture exact example text (don't paraphrase) for postmortem.
